_comment: Measured painted-line parking headings (degrees TRUE), used ONLY by static AIRCRAFT placement (GSE and infrastructure keep their own placement/orientation). pydcs does not expose the parking-slot heading, so static aircraft otherwise get a geometric guess. Where a field is listed here, its statics face the measured heading instead — exact facing with none of the AI-parked costs (no FPS hit, no map contacts, no pop-in). Fields not listed keep the geometric guess (nothing regresses).
_schema: map_key -> { airfield_name: VALUE }, where VALUE is either a NUMBER (one dominant heading for the whole field's majority apron) or an OBJECT { "default": <number>, "slots": { "<slot_name>": <heading>, ... } } for exact per-spot facing. Per-slot values win over default; default wins over the geometric guess. Slot names are the stable pydcs names (e.g. D15, A28) — read one in the Mission Editor on the parking-spot tooltip. Optional stands: {"<crossroad_idx>": {"slot_name": "02", "heading": 90.0, "x": 123.0, "y": 456.0}} binds exact directions to unique ids and source terrain coordinates; valid stands take precedence over legacy slot names.
_comment_slots: Removed 26 orphaned sub-slot measurements (names like '02-1', 'D09-1') on 2026-08-13. DCS names multi-aircraft stands parent-child; pydcs's terrain export flattens them to the parent, so those keys never resolved and the measurement was silently dead from the day it was taken. Every one was shadowed by a live measurement on its parent stand, and several DISAGREED with the parent by ~180 degrees (nose-in vs nose-out on the same spot), so keeping them would have been actively wrong if anything ever started resolving them. tests/test_parking_headings.py now fails on any such key.
